title: Finite exceptional adjunction on integral reduction mapping systems
statement:
Fix $k=\overline{\mathbf F}_q$ of characteristic $p$, a prime $\ell\ne p$, a finite extension $E/\mathbf Q_\ell$, its valuation ring $R$, a uniformizer $\varpi$, and $A_n=R/\varpi^n$ for $n\ge1$ [def-weil-finite-field-fiber, def-weil-l-adic-coefficient-extension]. On the small pro-etale site of a scheme $W$ put $B_{n,W}=(A_n)_W$ and $R_W=\lim_nB_{n,W}$ [def-weil-completed-integral-coefficients]. Use ordinary derived categories of module sheaves and the Roos-complete constructible category $D^b_c(W,R)$, whose finite reductions are constructible with a common bounded cohomological support [def-weil-derived-complete-integral-detailed, def-weil-derived-complete]. Write $P_n=P\otimes^L_{R_W}B_{n,W}$ [def-weil-integral-derived-reduction]. Use the strict semilinear coefficient-system category $\mathscr S_W$, the adjunction $\mathcal R_W\dashv\mathcal L_W$, its actual unit $u$ and counit $e$, and the mapping systems $\mathcal H_W$ of [lem-coef-derived-system-evaluation-calculus]; here $\mathcal R_WP=(P_n)_n$ with its coherent quotient maps and $\mathcal L_W=R\lim\operatorname{Res}$. Let $f:X\to Y$ be a separated finite-type morphism of separated finite-type $k$-schemes [def-weil-scheme-morphism-properties], and fix a compactification $f=pj$, with $j$ open and $p$ proper [def-nagata-compactification]. Use the functorial normalized finite-operation realizations $\mathcal F_f,\mathcal E_f$, the dualizing systems $\Omega_W$ and system duals $\mathcal D_W=\mathcal I_W(-,\Omega_W)$ of [lem-coef-finite-adjunction-diagram-realization].

Let $K\in D^b_c(X,R)$ and $L\in D^b_c(Y,R)$. Let $F_f=Rf_!=\mathcal L_Y\mathcal F_f\mathcal R_X$ be integral compact support [def-weil-integral-rational-qbar-compact-support] and set $J_f=\mathcal L_X\mathcal E_f\mathcal R_Y$. Then $F_fK\in D^b_c(Y,R)$. The actual coefficient-system counits are natural isomorphisms
$$c_K=e_{\mathcal F_f\mathcal R_XK}:\mathcal R_YF_fK\xrightarrow{\sim}\mathcal F_f\mathcal R_XK,\qquad c_L=e_{\mathcal E_f\mathcal R_YL}:\mathcal R_XJ_fL\xrightarrow{\sim}\mathcal E_f\mathcal R_YL.$$
The evaluations of $c_K$ are the canonical compact-support coefficient comparisons. Write $\mathcal A$ for the specified finite enriched adjunction of the diagram realization. There is a specified natural isomorphism in $D(\operatorname{Tow}(\operatorname{Ab}))$
$$\Psi_{K,L}=\mathcal H_X(1,c_L^{-1})\circ\mathcal A_{\mathcal R_XK,\mathcal R_YL}\circ\mathcal H_Y(c_K^{-1},1):\mathcal H_Y(\mathcal R_YF_fK,\mathcal R_YL)\xrightarrow{\sim}\mathcal H_X(\mathcal R_XK,\mathcal R_XJ_fL).$$
At level $n$, on degree-zero Hom and on every shifted Hom, this sends $u:(F_fK)_n\to L_n$ to
$$c_{L,n}^{-1}\circ\operatorname{adj}_n(u\circ c_{K,n}^{-1}):K_n\to(J_fL)_n,$$
where $\operatorname{adj}_n$ is the finite constructible exceptional adjunction [def-weil-exceptional-inverse-image, lem-coef-finite-exceptional]. Its finite mapping-complex isomorphism is the ordinary-etale enriched adjunction transported by the etale/pro-etale comparison, including the canonical compact-support comparison, and it respects the finite units, counits and all coefficient transitions. The map $\Psi$ is the displayed composite of actual derived-system transformations, not a lift selected merely from its evaluations. No integral adjunction is assumed.

proof.text: For an integral constructible input P, use its common cohomology interval [a,b]. The prime l is invertible in every residue field because it is invertible in D.k. Apply [lem-coef-integral-residue-tor] to bound the Tor amplitude of every actual finite reduction in [a,b]. The reduction_normalized field of [lem-coef-derived-system-evaluation-calculus] already supplies normalization of the actual system. Transport finite constructibility along the inverse of reductionEvaluation using isomorphism closure from [lem-weil-proetale-dbc-triangulated]. Transport Tor amplitude along the same isomorphism by composing the representative isomorphism in its defining test. These give exactly the two fields of the normalized finite-Tor domain of [lem-coef-finite-adjunction-diagram-realization].

source.place: Paragraph 2: domains of the finite mapping-complex adjunction

proof.text: For the two normalized output systems of [lem-coef-finite-adjunction-diagram-realization], apply purNormalizedReconstruction of [lem-pur-normalized-actual-reconstruction-maps]. The prime is a unit in global sections by mapping its unit in D.k through the structure morphism. This gives invertibility of the actual support and exceptional system counits, and completeness of the support limit. Convert the latter to intrinsic completeness by [lem-sf-derived-complete-legacy-comparison]. Compare every finite reduction of the support limit with the reduction of the already recorded constructible compact-support output of [def-weil-compact-support-finite-action]: compose reductionEvaluation inverse, evaluated support counit, supportEvaluation, compact support of the input reductionEvaluation, and the inverse recorded compact-support reduction comparison. Transport finite constructibility by [lem-weil-proetale-dbc-triangulated], and transport the same common support interval by homology of these isomorphisms. This proves support_and_counits without choosing an IntegralSupport or assuming any integral adjunction.

source.place: Paragraph 2: reduction of integral compact supports

proof.text: The previous step proves the actual system counits invertible. Their naturality is the existing adjunction counit naturality. To prove supportCoefficientComparison, apply the injective finite scalar-adjunction Hom equivalence to both sides. Right naturality and counit_projection identify the first transpose with the system projection followed by the restricted finite support comparison. The scalar-adjunction unit formula and naturality identify the other transpose with i.iso.hom followed by the finite scalar unit and restricted canonical support comparison. IntegralSupport.projections is precisely the equality of these transposes.

source.place: Paragraph 2: actual compact-support and exceptional counit identifications

proof.text: Apply the mapping bifunctors of [lem-coef-derived-system-evaluation-calculus] to $c_K^{-1}$ in the first variable and $c_L^{-1}$ in the second, and put between these maps the actual enriched isomorphism $\mathcal A_{\mathcal R_XK,\mathcal R_YL}$ of [lem-coef-finite-adjunction-diagram-realization]. The intermediate systems are $\mathcal H_Y(\mathcal F_f\mathcal R_XK,\mathcal R_YL)$ and $\mathcal H_X(\mathcal R_XK,\mathcal E_f\mathcal R_YL)$, so the composite has exactly the asserted source and target. Each factor is invertible; composing their inverses in reverse order gives its inverse. This defines the displayed $\Psi$ as a natural isomorphism of derived mapping systems before evaluation or limit.

source.place: Paragraph 2: middle mapping-complex isomorphism, conjugated by actual counits

proof.text: Use globalEvaluation_model from the existing resolution coherence of the specified calculi in [lem-coef-derived-system-evaluation-calculus]. Naturality of systemSectionsEvaluation followed by fiber_naturality proves globalEvaluation naturality on normalized inputs. Apply this to the support counit inverse and the exceptional counit inverse. Cancel the exceptional finite comparison in Enriched.finiteEvaluation from [lem-coef-finite-adjunction-diagram-realization]. Expanding the actual three-factor Psi, compose these three equations, cancel the intermediate globalEvaluation isomorphisms, and combine product morphisms by functoriality. This gives the displayed derived-category equality, hence all cohomological degrees. Apply H-zero; naturality of the fixed Hom equivalence in [def-coef-hom-zero-cycle-class] computes the two outside factors, and Enriched.finiteHom computes the middle factor as the finite adjunction of [lem-coef-finite-exceptional]. The result is c_L inverse after the finite adjunct of precomposition by c_K inverse. All maps remain system transformations before evaluation, retaining transitions and finite units and counits.

theorem integralExceptionalMappingSystem
    (CX : CoefficientDerivedSystemResolutionCoherence l E X SX)
    (CY : CoefficientDerivedSystemResolutionCoherence l E Y SY) (n : ℕ)
    (K : sfIntegralConstructibleCategory l E X) (L : sfIntegralConstructibleCategory l E Y) :
    finitePsi r a n K L =
      (coefficientFiniteGlobalHom l E Y n).map
        (Prod.mkHom ((finiteSupport r n K).inv.op) (𝟙 _)) ≫
      (a.finiteIso n).hom.app
        (op ((evaluation l E X n).obj ((R l E D hl X SX).obj K)),
          (evaluation l E Y n).obj ((R l E D hl Y SY).obj L)) ≫
      (coefficientFiniteGlobalHom l E X n).map
        (Prod.mkHom (𝟙 _) ((finiteExceptional r n L).inv)) ∧
    ∀ x : (DerivedCategory.homologyFunctor AddCommGrpCat.{u+1} 0).obj
        ((coefficientFiniteGlobalHom l E Y n).obj
          (op ((coefficientSequenceDerivedEvaluation l E Y n).obj
            (SY.reduction.obj ((F r).obj K))),
            (coefficientSequenceDerivedEvaluation l E Y n).obj (SY.reduction.obj L.obj))),
      coefficientFiniteHomEquiv l E X n _ _
        (((DerivedCategory.homologyFunctor AddCommGrpCat.{u+1} 0).map
          (finitePsi r a n K L)) x) =
      (((FiniteExceptional.adjunction l E D hl f c n).homEquiv
        ((evaluation l E X n).obj ((R l E D hl X SX).obj K))
        ((evaluation l E Y n).obj ((R l E D hl Y SY).obj L))
        (ObjectProperty.homMk ((finiteSupport r n K).inv ≫
          coefficientFiniteHomEquiv l E Y n _
            ((coefficientSequenceDerivedEvaluation l E Y n).obj
              (SY.reduction.obj L.obj)) x))).hom) ≫
        (finiteExceptional r n L).inv
